LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 PUNCTUATION: FULL STOP/CAPITAL LETTERS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Punctuation: Full Stop/Capital Letters
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.4.1 Punctuation: Full Stop/Capital Letters, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why do you use punctuation marks?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.4.1 Punctuation: Full Stop/Capital Letters together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: team work as learners work together in groups forming sentences using proper nouns.

● Digital literacy: creating with technology as learner manipulates digital devices to type sentences and text.

Values:
Unity: cooperation is developed as the learner is able to work together while they make coherent sentences.

Responsibility: determination is promoted as the learner makes a list of abbreviations and punctuates them.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion the learner is able to work in group activities as they make stickers with punctuated sentences.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate the concept of punctuation with the learning in Kiswahili.
